summary: The note summarizes the 1981 Disney animated drama The Fox and the Hound, based loosely on Daniel P. Mannix's novel. It follows a red fox named Tod and a hound named Copper, whose childhood friendship is pulled apart by their natural instincts and by hunter Amos Slade. The note also covers the film's release, budget, re-release, and direct-to-video sequel, and opens the story's second act as Tod learns to survive in the forest with help from Vixey and Big Mama.
one_line: A 1981 Disney animated drama about a fox and a hound whose childhood friendship is tested by their natural enmity, with release and sequel details.
key_facts: The Fox and the Hound is a 1981 American animated drama film produced by Walt Disney Productions.
The film is loosely based on the 1967 novel of the same name by Daniel P. Mannix.
The Fox and the Hound was the 24th Disney animated feature film.
The film was directed by Ted Berman, Richard Rich, and Art Stevens.
The film was released to theaters on July 10, 1981, and achieved financial success.
At the time of its release, The Fox and the Hound was the most expensive animated film produced to date, costing $12 million.
The film was re-released to theaters on March 25, 1988.
The direct-to-video followup, The Fox and the Hound 2, was released to DVD on December 12, 2006.
Big Mama the owl, with the help of Dinky the finch and Boomer the woodpecker, arranges for the orphaned red fox Tod to be adopted by Widow Tweed.
Widow Tweed names the fox Tod because he reminds her of a toddler.
Hunter Amos Slade brings home a hound puppy named Copper and introduces him to his hunting dog Chief.
After Slade threatens to kill Tod if he trespasses on his farm again, Big Mama, Dinky, and Boomer try to explain that Tod and Copper are natural enemies, but Tod refuses to believe them.
Tod's first night alone in the woods leads him into an irritable old badger's den, and a friendly porcupine offers him shelter.
Big Mama introduces Tod to a female fox named Vixey, and Vixey helps Tod adapt to life in the forest after the two foxes reconcile.
